text:
alex: Quick design chat — want to lock in the synthetic loadgen for runtime perf tests. Goal: exercise kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV-cache behavior so we catch regressions early. Thoughts on ramp/burst shapes and long-tail shaping?

maria: +1. We need both replay harnesses for real prefix distributions and synthetic patterns to force worst-case kernels. How do you want apples-to-apples?

alex: Apples-to-apples checklist: same model commit, same quantization, same CUDA/cuDNN/cuFFT driver, identical sequence-length distribution when comparing kernels, same GPU instance type, and identical server-side batching config. Also pin network/noise by running locally or in same AZ.

tyler: For the generator I propose 3 modes: replay (from production traces), synthetic-ramp (QPS ramp up -> steady -> ramp down), and bursty-longtail (background steady QPS + infrequent bursts + heavy-tail inter-arrival shaping). Config example:
```json
{
  "mode": "bursty-longtail",
  "steady_qps": 120,
  "burst": {"qps": 1200, "duration_s": 20, "interval_s": 300},
  "ramp": {"start_qps": 10, "end_qps": 120, "ramp_s": 120},
  "tail_shape": {"distribution": "pareto", "alpha": 1.5}
}
```

jess: FWIW we saw a perf regression last week where kernel selection fell back to slower kernel for seq_len>1024; p50 ok but p95 spiked. Any way to force the loadgen to hit that path deterministically?

alex: Yes — create a synthetic workload with 95% short-prefix (<512) and 5% long-prefix (>1024) but cluster long-prefix into bursts. That forces kernel switch and KV cache pressure at burst boundaries. Also add a 'cache-warm' phase to validate KV reuse vs miss penalties.

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot from last test (trimmed):
```
GPU kernels chosen: fused_attention_v2 (85%), attention_fallback (15%)
Avg batch size: 24
KV cache hits: 78% overall, during burst drops to 12%
P95 latency: baseline=142ms, during regression=512ms
```

maria: Nice. So generator needs to support: 1) controlled sequence-length mix, 2) burst clustering of long contexts, 3) warm/cold cache phases, 4) stochastic tail shaping. Plus an option to bind to a single model/binary to avoid kernel selection differences across runs.

tyler: Implementation notes: dynamic batching heuristic we want to test — current runtime uses fixed max_batch + adaptive flush-by-age. We should add backlog-aware batching: if backlog > threshold, allow larger batches even if age < flush_age. Pseudocode for decision:
```python
if backlog > backlog_high: target_batch = min(max_batch, backlog)
elif avg_latency > slo_ms: target_batch = max(1, floor(target_batch*0.75))
else: target_batch = min(default_batch, backlog)
```

jess: Also add a flag to disable kernel fallback during runs (force chosen kernel) so we can compare apples-to-apples between kernels. Useful to measure pure batching+cache impact without selection variance.

alex: Agreed. And add deterministic RNG seed for inter-arrival times when using pareto/exponential so runs are repeatable. For replay mode we should support rate-scaling factor to match target QPS while preserving temporal clustering.

maria: For metrics: capture per-request kernel_id, batch_size_at_dispatch, kv_hit_before, kv_hit_after, queue_time_ms, exec_time_ms, end_to_end_ms. Also record GPU SM utilization and PCIe stalls. We'll need lightweight exporter that doesn't perturb latencies.

perf-bot: Small tip — when profiling kernel selection, sample kernel timers on-device with CUPTI and correlate with request IDs (trace id) rather than relying solely on averages. That exposed a 30ms memcpy spike in prior run.

tyler: I'll prototype generator changes this week. Plan: add config-driven phases, seedable RNG, per-request metadata, and an option to inject synthetic prefixes from trace store. cc @jess for kernel-toggle API.

jess: I'll add a server-side param to lock kernel set per-worker. Also will add a KV-cache eviction sim flag to force miss patterns.

alex: Great. Next actions: tyler implement generator + perf tests; jess server flags; maria create apples-to-apples runbook and baseline configs; I'll run a matrix of (kernel_variant x batch_policy x cache_policy) and post results.

maria: One more thing — add CI gating: a quick smoke that runs short synthetic-burst and compares p95 to baseline; fail if regression > 25%. Keeps us from shipping regressions unnoticed. :hammer_and_wrench: 

alex: Love it. If anyone wants to pair on config schema ping me. We'll reconvene after the first end-to-end run. :rocket:
